question.text: Under the Fourth Schedule (Code of Conduct for AIFs) read with Reg 20A of SEBI (AIF) Regulations, an AIF Manager's obligations include ALL of the following EXCEPT:

answer.text: Operate and manage the fund in the interest of ALL investors (not only Sponsor or select class)
Guarantee minimum returns to all investors for the fund tenure
Maintain written policies to identify and mitigate conflicts of interest
Have written AML/CFT policies aligned with applicable laws

explanation.text: **The Logic:** The Fourth Schedule Code of Conduct requires AIFs to: (a) invest per PPM objectives, (b) operate in interest of ALL investors, (c) ensure dissemination of accurate and timely information, (d) maintain risk management and internal controls, (e) have written conflict-of-interest policies, (f) not use unethical marketing, (g) maintain AML policies. Guaranteeing returns is PROHIBITED — it violates the risk-sharing principle of AIF units and may constitute assured-return scheme under SEBI Act. **The Trap:** Option B appears 'investor-friendly' but is actually a serious regulatory breach. Guaranteed returns are classic features of Collective Investment Schemes, which AIFs are specifically exempt from structuring. Both the Fourth Schedule and SEBI Act Sec 11AA prohibit this. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C and XIX-A cover Code of Conduct. Compare with III-A/C Compliance, XXI-B PM Code of Conduct (similar conflict-management tests). NBFC/bank lending can promise fixed returns; AIF CANNOT. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** If an LP asks for a 'return floor' in negotiations, redirect to (i) hurdle rate with full catch-up (8%-100%-80/20), (ii) preferred return priority with waterfall, or (iii) a junior/senior unit structure with DFI sitting in first-loss tranche. Never promise guaranteed returns even informally — SEBI has banned AIF managers for this.
